classification.difficultyReason: Plot specified unit-circle points using angles of inclination, following a supplied demonstration.

content.prompt:
Identify these points on the unit circle, showing the radius and angle of inclination.
The first question has been done for you.

spec.description: Unit circle with double-arrowed axes, a visible radius at 70 degrees, coordinate label and counterclockwise angle indication.
spec.mathematics: The radius ends at (cos 70°, sin 70°) in quadrant I. The angle is measured counterclockwise from the positive horizontal axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied demonstration, visible in the student question.

answer.short: $(\cos70^{\circ},\sin70^{\circ})$, with radius $1$ and angle of inclination $70^{\circ}$.
answer.worked: Measure $70^{\circ}$ anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis and draw a radius of length $1$. Its endpoint has coordinates $(\cos70^{\circ},\sin70^{\circ})$, since $x=\cos\theta$ and $y=\sin\theta$.

answer.short: Quadrant I; radius at $25^{\circ}$ counterclockwise from the positive $x$-axis.
answer.worked: Draw a unit circle centred at the origin with coordinate axes. Measure $25^{\circ}$ counterclockwise from the positive $x$-axis and draw the radius. Label its endpoint $(\cos25^{\circ},\sin25^{\circ})$ and mark the $25^{\circ}$ angle.

spec.description: Completed unit-circle drawing with radius and endpoint in quadrant I and a 25-degree counterclockwise angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer evidence only; hidden from the student prompt.
